page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 48.77 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 34.91 GB/sec for large block write operations. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% of tested configurations.

From a resource density perspective, the t2d-standard-4 offers a cost-effective profile for workloads requiring dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a streamlined option for stateless applications. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight language model inference.
